analytics.bouncesHint: Bounces over Sent. Hard = permanent failures, soft = temporary ones, complaints = spam reports; every bounce is counted, so a subscriber with a hard and a soft bounce appears in both.
analytics.clientsHint: Email clients are recorded from the release of this feature onward; older activity shows as Unknown. Apple Mail includes its privacy proxy, which pre-fetches images, so its views are inflated by machine opens. A click is the browser the link opened in, not the mail client. Percentages are each client's share of the column in this table.
analytics.clientsTierHint: The tiers group the rows above. They are shown separately and are never added together: the sum would be a "real opens" figure this data cannot support. "From client software" is a ceiling on human opens, not a count of them — mail-security gateways pre-fetch with spoofed browser User-Agents and land here. "Via a provider proxy" means a real mailbox exists but the open timing is unreliable; Apple Mail sits here conservatively, because its privacy proxy and a real open cannot be told apart by User-Agent. "Declared machines" is non-interactive software (a link preview does mean a person shared the link). "No tier claimed" covers Other, the unnamed bare-Mozilla bucket and Unknown. On the Clicks column the tiers mean something weaker: a click's User-Agent is the browser the link opened in, so proxies barely appear and a browser click is usually a person — except that link-prefetching gateways also click, which is why "From client software" stays a ceiling on both columns.

analytics.conversions.hint: Sales, with the order count underneath. Both are attributed orders read side by side — never incremental lift. — means the campaign is not covered by that measure (a missing campaign is not zero); orders are counted by purchase time within the date range.

analytics.matrix.note: Campaigns with activity in the Mountain days from 60 days ago through today ({from} to {to}). A broadcast is listed when it started in that window, with everything recorded for it so far; a journey is listed when it sent in the window, with its sends and activity in the window only (each person counted once, on their first view or click). GP S% trails by a day or more, so today's rows show — there until it arrives; conversions are recomputed hourly (Tracked as fresh as the latest UTM export). %/$ shows every count over the row's Sent and conversions as sales; # shows counts and orders. Views are inflated by auto-opens (Apple MPP). Shop link attribution counts shop-link clickers by their shop-link kind (— = no shop link in the campaign). The Gmail gap is the Gmail proxy open rate over the Yahoo proxy open rate among the campaign's recipients (— for a journey); its rates accrue for about two days.
analytics.gmailGapOpens: Gmail open {gmailRate} ({gmailOpeners} of {gmail}) · Yahoo open {yahooRate} ({yahooOpeners} of {yahoo})
analytics.gmailGapHint: Gmail fetches images through its proxy only when a person opens, so Gmail's proxy open rate over Yahoo's (the control) says where Gmail put the mail: healthy ≈ 1, below {red} is bulking. Read it against the brand's previous campaigns, and after about two days.
analytics.gmailGapHintNoLine: Gmail fetches images through its proxy only when a person opens, so Gmail's proxy open rate over Yahoo's (the control) says where Gmail put the mail: healthy ≈ 1, well below that is bulking. Read it against the brand's previous campaigns, and after about two days.

analytics.locationHint: Location is recorded as of 29 Sept. 2026; older activity shows as Unknown. Views are located by the mail client's image proxy (Gmail, Apple Mail), so view countries skew toward the proxy's location, while clicks come from the reader's device. A subscriber seen in two countries counts once in each, so the columns need not add up to the totals above. Percentages are each country's share of the views or clicks in this table, not a rate over Sent.

series.welcomeDay0: Day 0 Welcome / Brand Introduction: Hero products and customer benefits, not a long brand story; deliver any promised signup incentive. Goal: a first purchase.
series.welcomeDay0Detail: Sends about 10 minutes after joining; a signup that is also a first order gets the Thank-you instead (item 3). Any paid order of the brand, before or after joining, exits the steps. CTA: SHOP [BRAND] or EXPLORE THE COLLECTION.
series.welcomeDay2: Day 2 Product Value / Why Choose Us: "Still exploring? Here's why [Brand] is different." Key product benefits and how the products fit everyday life, with one hero product or a small selection. Never a repeat of the welcome.
series.welcomeDay2Detail: Build interest and a reason to consider purchasing. Sent by the daily run two days after joining, to anyone with no paid order of the brand. CTA: DISCOVER [PRODUCT] or SHOP NOW.
series.welcomeDay5: Day 5 Build Confidence / Product Discovery: "A few reasons to feel good about your first order." Answer purchase questions or show approved customer feedback; without social proof, product discovery and existing offers. No artificial urgency.
series.welcomeDay5Detail: The most conversion-focused step. An offer (free shipping, or Kaylinn's 'buy 4, save 20%' example) appears only where the brand already runs it; no invented offer or urgency. CTA: FIND YOUR FAVORITES or SHOP NOW.
series.postPurchaseDay0: Day 0 First-Time Customer Welcome / Thank You: Thank them for choosing the brand, reinforce its value and set positive expectations. No sales pitch; no duplicate of the order confirmation Komigo sends.
series.postPurchaseDay0Detail: Enters on the first paid order ever with the brand, only if subscribed to the newsletter at the time (item 8); returning customers get nothing. CTA: EXPLORE [BRAND], only if relevant — this email may have no button.
series.postPurchaseDay5: Day 5 Getting Started / Delivery-Based: Around delivery: two or three practical first-use tips, simple instructions or answers to common questions, for a great first experience.
series.postPurchaseDay5Detail: Never ask about a product still in transit. CTA: GET STARTED or HOW TO USE.
series.postPurchaseDay14: Day 14 Get More From Your Purchase: Beyond the basics of Getting Started: more tips, techniques, routine ideas or ways to get more value from the product. Genuinely helpful, never a review request.
series.postPurchaseDay14Detail: Not another sales pitch; the sites have no review functionality. Per-brand examples are on the AI-generated Journey Campaigns page. CTA: EXPLORE MORE TIPS or DISCOVER MORE.
series.postPurchaseDay30: Day 30 Your Next Favorite / Second Purchase: A relevant reason to shop again (replenishment, another flavor or style, a complementary product, subscribing), tailored per brand. Skipped if they've ordered again.
series.postPurchaseDay30Detail: Not a universal restock email: the objective is the same on every brand, the purchase opportunity is Marketing's to tailor. CTA: FIND YOUR NEXT FAVORITE, REORDER NOW or SHOP MORE.

series.reengagementDay180: Day 180 Reconnect With the Brand: "Still want to hear from us?" Remind them what the brand offers, with hero products and a real reason to explore again.
series.reengagementDay180Detail: Sends the day someone is held: 180 days without a click, Gmail-confirmed open or purchase, after at least 6 broadcasts. No 'we miss you' copy without substance. One click on the button counts as engagement; Manage Preferences only as a second route. CTA: EXPLORE [BRAND].
series.reengagementDay270: Day 270 Another Reason to Reconnect: "Your emails are paused. Here's what you've been missing." A firmer reminder from a different angle: product variety, benefits or an evergreen re-engagement offer.
series.reengagementDay270Detail: 90 days after the hold. Never a repeat of the first ask. The button is a tracked link to the brand site (one click counts as engagement); Manage Preferences only as a second route. CTA: FIND YOUR FAVORITES or EXPLORE THE COLLECTION.
series.reengagementDay360: Day 360 Final Opportunity to Stay Connected: "Should we stop emailing you?" Say plainly that unless they respond within 5 days this is the brand's last marketing email.
series.reengagementDay360Detail: 180 days after the hold. The CTA must be an action the system counts as engagement: one click on the brand-site button is; the Manage Preferences link is not, only the tick on that page. CTA: STAY CONNECTED, with MANAGE PREFERENCES as a second route, never the only one.
series.reengagementDay365: Day 365 Inactivity Suppression: "We've stopped sending you marketing emails." A polite confirmation that the brand's marketing emails have stopped (suppressed, not unsubscribed), with a Manage Preferences button to facilitate resume.
series.reengagementDay365Detail: 185 days after the hold (a year without engagement at the default window). Outside Kaylinn's brief; the state and wording were settled 2026-11-08. No offers, no pitch, no guilt; the one step where Manage Preferences is the primary action.
dashboard.usage.reengagementHelp: The sunset schedule's four steps, each an automation on its own sunset queue list, sending at once: 180d the first ask (the day someone is held), 270d a second reminder, 360d the last chance, 365d the inactivity-suppression confirmation (days at the default 180-day window; the steps follow the hold at +90, +180 and +185 days). Each circle counts the automations on the re-engagement list in one state: green running, amber paused, grey draft or scheduled; red 0 when there is none (or no list) — cancelled and finished automations, and emails sent as broadcasts, do not count. A waiting language with no running automation shows in the hover and in the Skipped columns, not in the colour. Each circle opens its campaigns. Each step scores 5 with a running automation and 2 with only paused, draft or scheduled ones, like the other series.

settings.performance.batchSizeHelp: The number of subscribers to pull from the database in a single iteration. Each iteration pulls subscribers from the database, sends messages to them, and then moves on to the next iteration to pull the next batch. This should ideally be higher than the maximum achievable throughput (concurrency * message_rate).
settings.performance.cacheSlowQueriesHel: Only enable this on large databases that have slowed down significantly. Caches list subscriber counts, dashboard statistics etc.
settings.performance.concurrencyHelp: Maximum concurrent worker (threads) that will attempt to send messages simultaneously.
settings.performance.maxErrThresholdHelp: The number of errors (eg: SMTP timeouts while e-mailing) a running campaign should tolerate before it is paused for manual investigation or intervention. Set to 0 to never pause.
settings.performance.messageRateHelp: Maximum number of messages to be sent out per second per worker in a second. If concurrency = 10 and message_rate = 10, then up to 10x10=100 messages may be pushed out every second. This, along with concurrency, should be tweaked to keep the net messages going out per second under the target message servers rate limits if any.

settings.performance.slidingWindowRateHe: Maximum number of messages to send within the window duration.
